memory_update.text: LEU should remain the primary public reference asset for US HALEU enrichment exposure, but later layers must separate demonstration-scale HALEU from scalable commercial economics.
BWXT is a credible advanced-fuel/fabrication-adjacent reference candidate, but its large-cap, diversified defense nuclear profile reduces underfollowed purity.
LTBR and ASPI are discovery-lane speculative shadows: include only with explicit verification gates around licensing, irradiation/qualification, binding customers, DOE/NRC support, and funding.
The strongest US uranium conversion chokepoint appears embedded in Honeywell/ConverDyn rather than a clean pure-play listed company; this may be a negative investability conclusion for the node.

node: Nuclear fuel conversion, enrichment, HALEU production, and advanced fuel-cycle capacity
summary: Layer 1B expansion confirms the node is investable only through a thin and imperfect public universe. Centrus is the clearest US-listed HALEU/enrichment reference asset; BWX Technologies is a larger, better-known advanced nuclear fuel and component name with TRISO evidence; Lightbridge and ASP Isotopes are smaller speculative discovery candidates tied to advanced fuel or enrichment concepts but require much stronger verification before surviving later Serenity layers. The underfollowed insight remains partly negative: the tightest conversion bottleneck appears concentrated in assets such as Honeywell/ConverDyn Metropolis Works, but that exposure is embedded in a mega-cap and may be immaterial at the parent-company level.
